scope: Actual seven-image visual review of the regenerated final sixth-package Wrigley day/night overviews, field details, route7 at50seconds and1920x1200 night hero. Historical third-directory names are reused by the render script; image and executable hashes below identify this final package. This is not whole-movie acceptance.

findings: Southwest overview clearly shows the red marquee, open ballpark, green stands, outfield boards and Gallagher lawn.
The foreground neighboring roof is part of the mapped context and does not obscure the main landmark.
White field illumination, restrained roof surfaces, red marquee and warm plaza remain balanced.
Both blue video boards now show bright readable lettering; the manual board is visible as a lit green face. No renewed broad glowing roof band.
Bright stochastic speckles remain on parts of the warm plaza paving and some dark roof grain is visible at this sample budget; this review does not claim a noise-free still.
Unobstructed view across the playing field toward the ivy wall, bleachers, manual scoreboard and two screens.
White field markings, grass and dirt are distinct. Screen lettering remains legible in daylight after the night-material refinement.
Both video boards now have luminous blue faces and clearly readable white WRIGLEY FIELD text.
Manual scoreboard rows and green face are visibly illuminated across the board rather than only two small corner spots. Its small individual labels remain limited by viewing distance.
Field coverage remains even; the scoreboard adjustment does not create a new foreground hotspot or roof glow.
Elevated route view shows the exposed seating bowl, irregular outfield, light frames and nearby Gallagher plaza.
The nearer roof naturally occupies part of the lower frame during this aerial approach; the open field and opposite stands remain visible. No camera collision or corrupted geometry is apparent.
Night route frame retains the lit field, readable board faces, white light frames and warm plaza edge.
Roof remains subdued, with localized light falloff rather than the earlier overexposed continuous band. No conspicuous clipping, corruption or obstructing object crosses the camera.
Bright stochastic speckles remain on parts of the warm plaza paving and some dark roof grain is visible at this sample budget; this review does not claim a noise-free still.
Night hero clearly presents the red marquee with readable warm lettering, green field, white light frames, manual scoreboard and blue screens.
The broad roof remains subdued with localized lighting; Gallagher lawn and warm office/plaza provide foreground context without obscuring the stadium.

Bright speckles remain on portions of the plaza paving even at384samples, with fine dark-roof grain. They are recorded as a residual rendering limitation rather than described as intentional decorative lights. No new obstructing object, corrupted geometry or broad overexposed roof band is apparent.

acceptance: All seven current-package stills have coherent geometry, readable intended landmark features and clear intended camera framing.
The prior night roof/field imbalance and board-face readability issue remain corrected.
Residual plaza speckles and dark-surface grain remain visible; still acceptance does not assert perfect photorealism or zero noise.
limits: The scene remains an authored reconstruction, not a surveyed seat inventory, fixture schedule or current-game presentation.
Tiny manual-board labels are not individually readable from the wide field camera; its face, clock and row structure are visible.
The96/128sample galleries and384sample hero retain some bright plaza speckles and dark-surface grain. Denoised motion and final video encoding have separate acceptance records.
Only the seven identified stills were visually reviewed here. The Fisher Bridge ramp correction is elsewhere in the shared world and is outside this Wrigley visual scope.

independentManifestVerification.scope: CPU-only actual file hashing and read-only code-signature verification against the final manifests; no build, app launch or GPU dispatch.
